attempts.evidence: Pass 1 — full 2000x2294 colour raster. Legend carries the two declared rows and the strokes match their verdict classes (J1). Exactly ONE hourglass is drawn, green, on the bottom straight: `slow_steer` is a roll-rate cap that keeps the ideal line's turn-in station, so the two markers coincide and collapse to the owning line drawn last in role order (J2 — A-FIG82-SINGLEMARK holds). The scene declares no labels and no occluders, so J3 and J4 do not apply. The red line shares the turn point and then simply fails to turn: it holds a shallow arc, crosses the corridor edge before the corner develops and terminates "ran off" (J5).

Pass 2 — same raster, read for fabrication. Only declared ink: two lines, the one collapsed marker, the ladder/entry/outcome chrome, the scale bar. No fabricated marker, no sight ray on an unoccluded road (J7). Reading J5 strictly: the top-down alone shows "same turn point, did not turn", which is the honest visual half of slow steering; the rate itself is a lean-vs-station fact and lives in the controls strip, where the lean channel shows the roll-in still climbing at line end. Recorded as a pass with that reservation rather than a fail — the figure does not mislead, it under-shows.

Pass 3 — greyscale. The two strokes differ in weight and, decisively, in their captions: "clean" at the ideal arrowhead, "ran off" at the mistake terminal. The 10/20/30/40 m ladder and the scale bar stay readable; nothing depends on hue (J8).
